text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday morning's German newspapers:

- Chancellor Helmut Kohl says Germany's relations with Poland better than any time in the last century. Kohl met Polish President, Premier and other government leaders in Bonn in first German-Polish consultation, the first of a regular series of meetings planned.

- Defence Minister Volker Ruehe wants to create an integrated army unit with U.S. and French soldiers that would be used for international missions. Ruehe is negotiating with U.S. and French officials about the proposal.

- FDP insists on cutting the solidarity income tax surcharge. FDP takes reserved position to demands from eastern German CDU leaders urging delay in solidarity tax cut. FDP insists that Germans are determined to see the tax cut signal.
- Pound climbs back above three marks. Dollar and pound gains push shares to record levels. Decline in mark's value strengthens upturn in German shares.
- FDP insists on real tax cuts for Germans. Dispute over cutting solidarity tax creeps into coalition again.

- Rising dollar pushes German shares to record high levels. D-mark's decline against the dollar, pound and yen accelerate in dramatic fashion. Private investors turn increasingly to securities for their retirement funds. Stock market traders warn of price declines.
- Coalition cancels planned meeting on taxes with SPD. A planned meeting on Monday between coalition and SPD to find compromise on tax reform was cancelled because of dispute over scheduling.
- Telekom wins with every step. Sponsoring at Tour de France proves cost effective way to advertise, giving company wide media exposure without having to pay for expensive TV adverts.
- Germany supports Poland's bid to join EU. Germany starts new regular series of meetings with Poland that will be similar to regular German-French meetings.
- Berlin fights over Love Parade. Is it worldwide advertising for Berlin or an unacceptable burden for environment?
